title: One Empty Word Unlocked Ninety-Three Percent Yeses, Yet Raising the Cost Broke the Spell
description:
Myth vs. Neural Mechanism — Ellen Langer (1978): The Xerox Copy-Machine 'Because' Trick — 93% Let You Cut in Line for a Meaningless Reason!, grounded in Ellen J. Langer, Arthur Blank, Benzion Chanowitz (1978) (Journal of Personality and Social Psychology). Empirical findings show that in *1978 (Journal of Personality and Social Psychology), Ellen Langer, Arthur Blank, and Benzion Chanowitz sent confederates up to 120 busy people actively about to use the Xerox photocopier at the CUNY Graduate Center library with three nearly identical phrasings*.

Follow-up physiological and behavioral evidence demonstrates: When the favor was SMALL (cutting in to copy 5 pages): Asking with Request Only ('Excuse me, I have 5 pages. May I use the Xerox machine?') succeeded 60% of the time.

Primary Peer-Reviewed Sources:
- Ellen J. Langer, Arthur Blank, Benzion Chanowitz (1978). The mindlessness of ostensibly thoughtful action: The role of "placebic" information in interpersonal interaction. Journal of Personality and Social Psychology. https://doi.org/10.1037/0022-3514.36.6.635
- Valerie S. Folkes (1985). Mindlessness or mindfulness: A partial replication and extension of Langer, Blank, and Chanowitz. Journal of Personality and Social Psychology. https://doi.org/10.1037/0022-3514.48.3.600
- Ellen J Langer (1992). Matters of mind: Mindfulness/mindlessness in perspective. Consciousness and Cognition. https://doi.org/10.1016/1053-8100(92)90066-j
